seed.name: neonatal intrahepatic cholestasis due to citrin deficiency

partners.mechanism_chain: SLC25A13 (HGNC:10983) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial aspartate/glutamate carrier (AGC1) function (REACT:R-HSA-75927); Mitochondrial aspartate/glutamate carrier (AGC1) function (REACT:R-HSA-75927) —DISRUPTS→ Citrate transport between mitochondria and cytosol; Citrate transport between mitochondria and cytosol —DECREASES→ Urea cycle (REACT:R-HSA-70271); Urea cycle (REACT:R-HSA-70271) —DECREASES→ Ammonia detoxification; Ammonia detoxification —DECREASES→ Hyperammonemia (HP:0012744); Citrate transport between mitochondria and cytosol —DECREASES→ Intrahepatic cholestasis (HP:0001349). Mutations in SLC25A13 impair the function of the mitochondrial aspartate/glutamate carrier (AGC1), disrupting the transport of aspartate and glutamate across the inner mitochondrial membrane. This affects the malate-aspartate shuttle and thus citrate transport out of the mitochondria. Impaired citrate export disrupts the urea cycle, leading to hyperammonemia (characteristic of citrullinemia type II), and also impacts fatty acid and cholesterol synthesis, contributing to intrahepatic cholestasis (characteristic of neonatal intrahepatic cholestasis due to citrin deficiency).
